haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store. It never charges and never writes the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive clean days, 5,000+ invoices compared (scope unsettled), zero unresolved mismatches at move time. A person requests it; the controller enforces the gate.
haiku-low.q4: The charge failure monitor's rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only (before day 35). How the controller learns of it is not defined.
haiku-low.q5: Always old_only, after R1 to R5 pass and the flip. Gates reset to zero, so the new engine must pass shadow again before taking over.
haiku-low.q6: After day 35, because usage events expire at 35 days and R3 needs the skipped events to reprocess; old engine retirement also starts then.
haiku-low.q7: Engines re-read billing_mode before every charge and ledger write. If unreadable, they queue the charge without a claim and retry. Mid-invoice handling: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Daily comparison results sit in the shadow store; the controller reads them to update gate counters. The controller refuses any forward move whose gate is unmet.
haiku-low.q9: The charge failure monitor measures the new engine's failed charge attempt rate per rolling 10-minute window. Above 2%, it starts rollback automatically.
haiku-low.q10: Due charges queue with amount, no claim. Closed periods are charged in R4; open periods and queued rows after the flip.
haiku-low.q11: The per-(customer, billing period) claim in the ledger: a conditional create fails if a successful or pending claim exists. Idempotency keys stop provider double-charges.
haiku-low.q12: Left in blocked_rollback: step and reason recorded, alert sent, freeze still set. On-call resumes by re-running that whole step, or aborts back to origin.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store. It never charges and never writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
sonnet.q3: Seven consecutive clean days, at least 5,000 invoices compared (per day or across the window is unsettled, so the gate cannot be evaluated yet), and zero unresolved mismatches at the time of the move. A person asks the rollout controller to make the move, and the controller writes the flag. Who that person is is not defined.
sonnet.q4: Auto rollback starts when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2 percent in any 10-minute window. It can happen in both and new_only (new_only only before day 35). It never happens in shadow. How the trigger reaches the controller is not defined.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, at the flip. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout has to go forward through shadow again. The flip resets all gates, so the 7-day clean count starts over, and the rollout must then pass the shadow to both gate and then the both to new_only gate.
sonnet.q6: It stops being possible after day 35 in new_only. The usage event log is kept only 35 days, and R3 needs the skipped events from that log. Expired events block the rollback. The old engine can also be retired at day 35 if no rollback is running.
sonnet.q7: Both engines read billing_mode fresh from the config service before every charge attempt and every ledger write, with no caching. For an invoice being processed at that moment, the document says what protects against double charges. The charge claim check in the ledger still applies even if an engine acts on a stale read, so at most one successful charge is made per customer and billing period. It does not describe other handling of an in-flight invoice. A worker that cannot read the flag does not charge. It queues the due charge with no claim and raises an alert.
sonnet.q8: The evidence is the nightly comparison results in the shadow store: one result per day with invoices compared, mismatches and unresolved mismatches. The controller reads them to update gate counters in the rollout record, and the rollout record also holds the Finance sign-off. The controller refuses a forward move and names the unmet condition if the gate is not met, a rollback is running or blocked, or another move is pending.
sonnet.q9: The charge failure monitor detects it. It checks the new engine's resolved charge attempts in each rolling 10-minute window. The rate is failures divided by attempts, and a failure is a decline, a timeout that resolves as not charged, or an engine error. When the rate is above 2 percent in both or new_only, it starts the rollback automatically. How the controller learns of the trip is not defined, and no minimum attempt count is set.
sonnet.q10: The freeze marker is set in R1. Charges that fall due from either engine are queued with the customer, period, amount due and invoice reference, and no claim is created. The rollback job charges closed periods in R4. Queued rows for open periods are charged by normal processing after the flip. Queued rows are drained through the old engine after the freeze is cleared, at their stored amounts. After an abort, queued rows go to the engine of the origin mode. Open periods wait until they close.
sonnet.q11: The charge claim in the billing ledger stops it. It allows at most one successful charge per customer and billing period, whichever engine makes it. In R4, a closed period with a successful claim is not re-charged, even if the old engine's invoice amount differs. A difference is caught as a mismatch in R5. The claim check still applies on a stale flag read.
sonnet.q12: If a step fails, the rollback goes to blocked_rollback. The controller records the blocked step and reason and sends an alert. The flag still holds the origin, because it is not written until the flip. The freeze marker stays set, so normal charging is suspended and due charges queue. Claims already made stay. The rollback stays blocked until on-call acts. On-call can resume after fixing the cause. The controller re-checks that step's precondition and re-runs only that step. Earlier steps are not re-run, and the claim checks prevent double charging. On-call can abort instead. Abort clears the freeze, returns the rollout record's mode to the origin, and the origin's engines resume. If the flag write at the flip fails, the rollback stays at R5 complete with the freeze set and the controller retries.
